name: Permissive CORS: wildcard or reflected Access-Control-Allow-Origin
attack_scenario: A malicious page makes a credentialed fetch() to the victim API; because the origin is reflected and credentials allowed, the attacker's JavaScript reads the authenticated response (account data, tokens) cross-origin.
negative_test_hint: send a credentialed cross-origin request with Origin "https://evil.example.com" and assert the response carries no matching Access-Control-Allow-Origin header

exemplar.explanation: Setting Access-Control-Allow-Origin to '*' or blindly reflecting the request Origin ($http_origin / %{HTTP_ORIGIN}) lets any website read cross-origin responses, and reflection typically pairs with Allow-Credentials: true, defeating the same-origin policy for authenticated endpoints. Pinning the header to an explicit allowlisted origin keeps credentialed responses same-origin-only.
